question.text: During Brahmaputra Credit Fund's DD, the LP team requests details on how the Fund handles 'potential conflicts of interest' on co-investment allocation. The Manager runs 3 parallel funds (Fund II main, a direct-lending sidecar, and a GIFT IFSC feeder). Per Ch 12's conflict-mitigation framework, the Manager's co-investment allocation policy should:

answer.text: Disclose in the PPM; allocate pro-rata to fund AUM with documented IC minutes; offer co-invest rights to LPs transparently on equal terms; avoid giving affiliate entities preferential co-invest pricing different from the Fund; and include the policy in the conflict-resolution section of the PPM.
Prioritise the GIFT IFSC feeder since foreign capital gets lower Indian tax cost.
Allocate all deals to Fund II first and only sidecar overflow deals go to the direct-lending vehicle.
Make all allocation decisions at the sole discretion of the Managing Partner without IC involvement.

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 12's 'Mitigation of Conflict of Interest' lists: disclose in PPM; do not favour affiliates on different terms; Manager's sole-discretion co-invest only where terms are identical to Fund's; PPM must include conflict-resolution policy. The Trap: B, C, D all introduce conflicts/favouritism without proper governance and documentation. Cross-Exam Context: Co-invest allocation is a classic GP-LP negotiation — parallels with 'aggregation and allocation' in XXI-B (PM) for multi-account managers. Manager's Pro-Tip: Run a quarterly 'Allocation Committee' with an independent member (e.g., an LP Advisory Board observer). Minutes should show: deals sourced, allocation rationale, co-invest offers made, LP acceptances. This single practice kills 80% of LP conflict concerns.
